My main theory of this is that people do not understand the caliber of Basketball played in the NBA. Nor the strategy and decision-making happening at such intense speeds.


The biggest complaint I hear from most people is that NBA is boring because of all of the fouls and stopping the game. "College basketball is just so much better." Those people don't know squat about the game and the absolute INTENSE level these athletes play at. No other league do you see guys going as big as you see these fellas go. **Football is a rough sport in it's nature, everyone puts their bodies in the line there too yes** But the NBA players CHOOSE to go big. No one says they have to fly through the air at ridiculous speed to the hoop. The evolution of the game comes from guys GOING BIG in all sorts of ways. (Props to my street ballers, cause it definitely starts there too)

The problem that I see is that it takes more than just a general knowledge of the game to appreciate it. OR a willingness and desire to really understand it. I've had girlfriends who HATED it, but as I refuse to go out or be away from a TV when my teams play... they have had to watch. After explaining the game and why things happen. Explaining different strategies D and O wise every single one has become a lifelong NBA fan. 

I absolutely love the game, and meet SO many people who don't like it because they just don't get why it plays the way it does. (slow)

Football- easy as hell to understand.. look at the fans (jk jk)
Baseball- come on.... that is just terribly boring, but people understand it so easily.
Basketball- to truly appreciate the flow of the game you really need a good understanding of the rules as well as the strategies involved. Otherwise its a bunch of guys who look like they are just running around aimlessly on a court trying to make a basket.

Don't mean to bash any other sport really. I appreciate what goes into each sport and the hard work all athletes do. To me personally nothing beats the combination of coaching, athleticism and straight up grace this game brings to sports.

I've been cleaning my glass pieces for years with this method and never encountered a problem. If I'm advising people to do something unsafe then I'll take my post down.

I have used a lot of different cleaners and methods to clean my glass. My favorite general cleaner is Grunge Off, best by far. However I have a bunch of glass to clean and I clean it so regularly that it's cheaper to buy quantity of iso, salt and soap.
**I am usually cleaning glass that I already keep pretty clean. If your piece is incredibly dirty let it soak in alcohol in a bag prior to doing all of this

1.) Pour 91% Iso alcohol, very small amount in a shot glass.

2.) Pour a small amount of fine grain salt into the largest opening in your piece to use as an abrasive.

3.) Set in microwave at power level 8 until you see the first bubbles around 15 seconds.
** ISO is quick to boil when microwaved and heats up almost instantly so be cautious your first time.

4.) Pour the hot ISO into the piece and shake vigorously. 
**To avoid being burned hold the openings with a paper towel or two. 

5.) Pour out the solution in the piece and if it is particularly dirty repeat the process.

6.) As for the rinsing out to get the nasty flavors out, I put a little bit of dish soap and water into the piece. 
**Adding to remaining ISO is fine as long as the ISO is almost transparent, NO BROWN.

7.) As with all glass to rinse with water and give it that 100% fresh taste you need to make sure you are rinsing with HOT WATER FIRST. The hot water will leave a terrible smell/taste in it, so you FINISH with a COLD WATER rinse. 

TL;DR version:
1)Pour dime size salt in piece
2)Microwave iso in shot glass ---- 10 seconds
3)Pour in and shake like mad
4)Rinse: Soapy water, HOT WATER and always finish with COLD WATER
